marketPlan: United States first; expand internationally only where the final product is permitted and supported.
scope: FYNX is its own product. Owner crypto tools support Ethereum Sepolia and Base Sepolia test transactions, plus read-only Base mainnet. Public access stays on the waitlist. No MoonPay integration is planned.

items.title: One FYNX website and a live waitlist
items.current: GitHub hosts the public site and owner dashboard. Firebase stores confirmed registrations with consent and retention metadata.
items.next: Maintain the waitlist until the public-launch gates are approved.

steps.text: Public website and waitlist published from GitHub Pages.
Registrations saved with consent, notice version and a 365-day expiry.
On your phone, open the public website, join the waitlist with a test address ending in @example.com and confirm the success message.
In the Waitlist tab, find that test address, check its consent details, then remove it.

items.title: Account login and recovery
items.current: Google, email/password and passkeys are implemented for the verified owner. Virtual passkey and authorization tests passed.
items.next: Test Google, email recovery, passkey creation/sign-in/removal, and browser attestation on actual supported devices. Account recovery does not recover wallet funds.

steps.text: Google, email/password and passkey sign-in built; virtual passkey and owner-only authorization tests pass.
Sign in with Google in a normal (not private) desktop browser. Note the browser and version.
Use “Set or reset an email password”, open the email, set a password, then sign in with email and password.
Account security → Add a passkey on this computer and confirm it appears in the list.
Sign out, then sign back in with “Use a passkey”.
Add a passkey on your iPhone or iPad in Safari and sign in with it.
Remove one passkey and confirm it can no longer be used to sign in.
Leave the workspace untouched for 15 minutes and confirm it signs you out.
Try to sign in with a Google account that is not the owner and confirm access is refused.

items.title: Separate accounts for every customer
items.current: Public customer accounts are deliberately closed; the backend authorizes one owner.
items.next: Implement per-user profiles, wallet ownership, session revocation, abuse limits and cross-account isolation tests on the selected production infrastructure. Open registration only after approval.

steps.text: Per-customer profiles and wallet ownership records.
Cross-account isolation tests: one customer can never read or act on another’s data.
Session revocation, rate limits and abuse controls for public sign-up.
Approve opening registration only after the security, legal and pilot gates pass.

items.title: Wallet creation and recovery
items.current: Version one connects an existing user-controlled wallet. FYNX does not create a wallet, generate 24 words, or recover signing keys from email.
items.next: Prove external-wallet recovery first. If creating a wallet inside FYNX is required, select and independently review key generation, encrypted storage, device/passkey access, backup, export and recovery before implementation. Never ask users for an existing Ledger phrase.

steps.text: Version one connects an existing wallet; FYNX never creates, stores or asks for recovery words.
Decide: is connecting your own wallet (for example MetaMask or Ledger) enough for launch, or must FYNX create wallets inside the app? Write your decision in the note.
Restore a test wallet from its recovery phrase in that wallet’s own app (never on FYNX) and confirm the same address appears in Crypto tools.
Only if FYNX must create wallets: independent review of key generation, encrypted storage, backup, export and recovery before any build.

items.title: Send, receive and signing
items.current: ETH and canonical USDC test transfers have address/network/fee review, token simulation, bounded amounts, one-use approval and receipt lookup. Receive QR codes include the chain and asset. Real contracts executed successfully in an isolated Base Sepolia fork.
items.next: Record physical-wallet approval/rejection, public testnet transfers and independent recipient balances. Test recovery and supported browsers/devices. Mainnet signing remains disabled.

steps.text: ETH and USDC transfers with review, simulation, limits and receipts passed on an isolated Base Sepolia copy.
Sending on Base mainnet is blocked; only test networks can sign.
In a wallet that holds no real money, get free Base Sepolia test ETH from a faucet listed in Base’s documentation.
Crypto tools → Base Sepolia → Connect wallet → Review ownership message → approve. Confirm the wallet shows as verified.
Repeat, but reject the ownership signature in the wallet. Confirm the page says nothing was approved.
Scan the Receive QR code with a phone wallet and confirm the address and network match exactly.
Send 0.001 test ETH to a second address you control. Note the transaction ID and confirm the recipient balance on the Base Sepolia block explorer.
Send 1 test USDC the same way (test USDC comes from Circle’s testnet faucet).
Start a transfer and reject it in the wallet. Confirm nothing was sent.
Repeat one transfer with a Ledger, approving on the device screen.
Switch to Base mainnet and confirm sending and swapping stay disabled.

items.title: Live assets, balances and transaction history
items.current: Live ETH/USDC balances on Ethereum Sepolia, Base Sepolia and read-only Base. Session transaction journal and hash lookup are implemented. The separate dashboard remains a simulation.
items.next: Add complete indexed transaction history, reliable production RPC/failover, replacement/reorg handling and market prices. Bitcoin and Solana are not implemented.

steps.text: Live ETH and USDC balances on Ethereum Sepolia, Base Sepolia and Base (read-only).
Session transaction list and transaction lookup.
Compare the balances shown in Crypto tools with the block explorer on both test networks.
Paste a transaction ID into “Track confirmation” and confirm the status matches the explorer.
Complete transaction history from an indexing provider.
Production network connection with a backup provider if the first fails.
Handle replaced, dropped and reorganised transactions.
Market prices from a licensed data provider.

items.title: Buy and sell through cards or bank accounts
items.current: A server-only Transak sandbox checkout and order-status adapter is implemented with fixed hosts, verified-wallet binding and private secrets. No partner credentials are supplied; it fails closed. No live payments are enabled.
items.next: Create a provider sandbox account, enable BUY/SELL, arrange required IP allowlisting and supply staging credentials in Secret Manager. Test purchases, sales, cancellations, refunds and reconciliation. Business approval, production credentials and legal review are separate gates.

steps.text: Transak sandbox checkout and order check built; stays off until credentials are added.
Create a Transak partner account and get its staging (test) API key and access token. Never paste them into chat or GitHub.
Transak approves the backend’s fixed IP address (needs a static outbound address set up first).
Put the staging key in Google Cloud Secret Manager (FYNX_TRANSAK_SANDBOX), following docs/PROVIDER-SETUP.md.
Redeploy only the owner function so it picks up the new secret.
Crypto tools → Check integration status, then create a sandbox Buy and a Sell checkout, and verify each order ID.
Test a cancelled and a failed sandbox order and confirm they never show as paid.
Provider business approval, production contract and legal review before real payments.

items.title: Swap assets safely
items.current: Direct ETH/USDC Uniswap v3 swaps on Base Sepolia: bounded slippage/price impact, one-minute quotes, exact/reset/revoke approvals, simulation and on-chain minimum output. Base mainnet quotes are read-only. Local-fork swaps passed in both directions.
items.next: Verify public-testnet and hardware-wallet execution; independently review the pinned contracts, pricing/manipulation risks, routing, fee handling and production release policy. Mainnet swaps stay disabled.

steps.text: ETH ↔ USDC swaps with slippage, price-impact, expiry and minimum-received limits passed on an isolated Base Sepolia copy.
Crypto tools → Base Sepolia → get a quote for 0.001 ETH → USDC and check the minimum received.
Complete that swap in your wallet and confirm both balances on the explorer.
Swap a small amount of USDC back to ETH: approve the exact amount, request a fresh quote, swap.
Use “Revoke swap allowance” and confirm the allowance is zero.
Repeat one swap approving on a Ledger.
Independent review of the pinned contracts, pricing risks and fee handling before real funds.

items.title: Production security and independent audit
items.current: Owner authorization, App Check, challenge replay protection, dependency checks and an internal review are in place. Current GitHub origin and Firebase project are shared with other applications.
items.next: Choose a dedicated production origin/backend boundary, configure response headers and secrets/IAM, retest App Check on normal browsers, and commission an independent signing/auth review with fixes and retesting.

steps.text: Owner-only authorization, App Check, replay protection, dependency checks and an internal review.
Choose a dedicated web address and a separate Firebase project for the production wallet.
Security headers, secrets and access permissions on that dedicated setup; retest App Check in normal browsers.
Choose and hire an independent security reviewer for signing and sign-in.
Independent review completed, issues fixed and retested.

items.title: Publish only verified releases
items.current: The Pages workflow waits for tests, generated-file checks and dependency audits. Only approved public assets are packaged, with a revision/hash manifest.
items.next: Keep deployment gated; use the published manifest and Actions run to identify each release. Backend deployments and rollbacks remain separately scoped.

steps.text: Website updates publish only after tests, generated-file checks and dependency audits pass.
Each release publishes a revision and file-hash manifest.
Open the GitHub Actions page and confirm the latest “Verify and publish FYNX Wallet” run is green.

items.title: Monitoring, backups and incident recovery
items.current: Audit retention, rate limits, a connection check and an incident procedure exist. There is no tested alert recipient or restore drill.
items.next: Assign monitored support/security contacts, set failure/authorization/billing alerts, test delivery, select backup retention and recovery objectives, and restore into an isolated environment. Connection checks are not continuous monitoring.

steps.text: Audit retention, rate limits, connection checks and a written incident procedure.
Name who reads fynxteam5@gmail.com every day, and a backup person.
Choose where alerts go (email or phone) for failures, sign-in problems and billing.
Set up those alerts in Google Cloud and send a test alert.
Choose how long backups are kept and how quickly the service must be restored after an outage.
Restore a backup into a separate test project and record the result.
Walk through the incident procedure once with your team (a 30-minute practice run).

items.title: U.S. launch permissions and consumer protections
items.current: The owner supplied the name FYNX finance world inc. and selected the United States as the first intended market. Incorporation state, registration details and legal permissions are unverified.
items.next: Confirm entity details and the exact custody/payment model. Have counsel determine federal/state licensing, AML/KYC, sanctions, age/eligibility, privacy, consumer terms, disclosures and complaints duties. Finish the required registrations, contracts and controls before serving customers.

steps.text: Confirm FYNX finance world inc.’s state of incorporation and registration details.
Confirm the model: customers keep their own keys and a licensed provider handles card and bank payments.
Hire qualified U.S. counsel experienced with crypto and payments.
Counsel reviews federal and state licensing, anti-money-laundering, sanctions, age and eligibility, privacy and complaints duties.
Customer terms, privacy notice and risk disclosures drafted and approved.
Complete the registrations and contracts counsel requires.

items.title: International availability
items.current: Worldwide access is a future goal, not current eligibility or authorization.
items.next: Approve each country and product separately for local requirements, sanctions, payment/provider coverage, data handling and support. Implement an approved-country policy before expansion; do not promise all countries.

steps.text: Pick the first country after the U.S.
Counsel and payment provider confirm what is allowed and supported in that country.
An approved-country list that blocks sign-up from anywhere not approved.

items.title: Controlled public launch
items.current: Public customers remain on the waitlist. No launch date, real-funds readiness or flawless operation is claimed.
items.next: After the applicable gates pass, run a small approved pilot with limits, staffed support, recovery/incident procedures, reconciliation, measured reliability and a rollback decision. Obtain explicit owner release approval before removing the waitlist.

steps.text: Decide the pilot: how many people, which states, and the maximum amounts.
Arrange who answers support during the pilot, and how fast.
A tested rollback plan and reconciliation reports for the pilot.
Give final written approval to remove the waitlist for the pilot group.
